task: Add a default-off allow_user_context opt-out on both the MCP path (two-level precedence: MCPServerConfigData server default overridden per-assistant on MCPServerDetails, enforced in MCPConnectClient._build_request_payload) and the DSP path (single flat boolean on Provider/ProviderBase, enforced in ProviderToolFactory.invoke()).

key_reasoning.reason: 4+ components across two sibling subsystems — MCP (MCPServerConfigData persistence, MCPServerDetails assistant config, MCPToolkitService/_build_request_payload runtime enforcement) and DSP (ProviderBase persistence, ProviderToolFactory.invoke() runtime enforcement) — plus a confirmed new abstraction needed: MCPExecutionContext is built once per get_mcp_server_tools call but enforcement must vary per server/per-assistant-tool.

No in-family precedent for a boolean enable/disable gate on either model (closest MCP analog, headers/env, is an additive merge, not a toggle; DSP has no gating precedent at all). The field governs whether PII-bearing user_context (email, roles, admin flags) reaches an external MCP-Connect/DSP provider server, which is privacy/security-sensitive — Security red flag applied, bumping base L (4) to XL (5).

~7 source files (mcp_config.py, assistant.py, toolkit_service.py, mcp/models.py, client.py, provider.py, provider_tool_factory.py) plus a comparable set of test files (test_models.py, test_execution_context_integration.py, mcp_config_service tests, test_assistant_model.py, test_provider_tool_factory.py, test_provider_service.py) spanning rest_api/models, service/mcp, service/provider and tests/ — 3+ directories, no new files.

Defaults and enforcement points are explicit for both paths, but three confirmed design gaps are open: the MCPServerDetails->MCPServerConfig translation step was never traced in research, the shared per-call MCPExecutionContext needs to become per-server-aware (no design decided), and ProviderService.update()'s truthy-only field-copy may silently drop an explicit False on update.

API (config/assistant create-update-response models), Service (MCPToolkitService, ProviderToolFactory), DB-Persistence (MCPConfig and Provider JSONB columns), and External (the payload MCP-Connect and DSP providers receive changes) — 4 layers, backend-only, no UI layer.

red_flags_applied: Security requirement (gating PII-bearing user_context sent to external MCP-Connect/DSP provider servers) bumped Technical Risk from L (4) to XL (5)
